content:
According to a recent Guardian report, Apple is in negotiations for the US broadcast rights to The Open Championship. Netflix and Amazon are also reportedly interested in those broadcast rights.

The Open Championship was first held in Scotland in 1860 and is the oldest of the four men's golf major championships, organised by The R&A. Americans occasionally refer to the event as the "British Open" to distinguish it from the separately held U.S. Open.

In 2017, NBC outbid ESPN at a higher price and signed a 12-year broadcast rights deal with The Open Championship. Versant also holds a portion of the broadcast rights and operates the Golf Channel. The R&A said it expects to hold discussions with NBC and Versant, as well as other parties interested in the broadcast rights.

Today's report indicated that Apple and The R&A have held "preliminary discussions" regarding the bidding for The Open Championship broadcast rights. The report cited a source "familiar with Apple's plans" and noted that Apple "remains committed to investing in sports broadcast rights and will continue to look for suitable sports assets".

A spokesperson for The R&A responded to the Guardian as follows:

"Our partnership with NBC and Versant has always been a very pleasant one, bringing significant benefits to The Open Championship, the AIG Women's Open, and our other events and international activities. Looking ahead to The R&A's next round of US media rights, we expect to engage with our existing partners NBC and Versant at the appropriate time. We will also continue to monitor the ever-changing broadcast landscape and the broad interest from various parties in our broadcast rights."

Last year, Apple announced a major partnership with F1, becoming F1's exclusive broadcast partner in the United States. The company also broadcasts Friday Night Baseball and Major League Soccer (MLS) matches.
